contracts.text: A new module `psd_tools.api.blend_range` exists.
`BlendRangeChannel` class is defined in `psd_tools.api.blend_range`.
`BlendRangeChannel` has a mutable attribute `this_layer_black`.
`BlendRangeChannel` has a mutable attribute `this_layer_white`.
`BlendRangeChannel` has a mutable attribute `underlying_black`.
`BlendRangeChannel` has a mutable attribute `underlying_white`.
Each of the four attributes (`this_layer_black`, `this_layer_white`, `underlying_black`, `underlying_white`) is a `(left_handle, right_handle)` tuple.
Each handle value in the tuples is in the range 0–255.
contracts.adverse_condition: Boundary values 0 and 255 are used; out-of-range values are supplied.

contracts.text: `BlendRangeChannel.from_raw(raw_pair)` classmethod or staticmethod exists.
`from_raw` accepts a 2-element list of `(black_uint16, white_uint16)` pairs.
In `from_raw`, the low byte of each uint16 encodes the left handle and the high byte encodes the right handle.
contracts.adverse_condition: High bytes are non-zero and differ from low bytes (split sliders), so swapping byte order would be detectable.

contracts.text: Positional: in `from_raw`, the first element of the list maps to the black handles and the second element maps to the white handles.
contracts.adverse_condition: The black and white uint16 pairs are distinguishable (different values).

contracts.text: `BlendRangeChannel.to_raw()` method exists.
`to_raw()` converts a `BlendRangeChannel` back to the 2-element list of uint16 pairs, round-tripping with `from_raw`.
contracts.adverse_condition: High bytes are non-zero (split sliders); trivial zero-high-byte cases could succeed accidentally.

contracts.text: `BlendRangeChannel.default()` classmethod returns a `BlendRangeChannel` at full range.
`BlendRangeChannel.from_values(this_layer_black, this_layer_white, underlying_black, underlying_white)` classmethod or staticmethod exists.
All four parameters of `from_values` default to full range.
`from_values` creates non-split channels: for every resulting `BlendRangeChannel`, `left_handle == right_handle` for all four sliders.
contracts.adverse_condition: Explicit non-equal handle values are passed to `from_values`.

contracts.text: Positional: each of the four `from_values` arguments maps to its correct attribute (`this_layer_black`, `this_layer_white`, `underlying_black`, `underlying_white`) in order.
contracts.adverse_condition: All four arguments are pairwise distinguishable and the mapping is non-commutative.

contracts.text: `BlendRangeChannel.is_default` property exists.
`is_default` returns `True` when all handles are at their default (full-range) positions.
`is_default` returns `False` when any handle is not at its default position.
contracts.adverse_condition: At least one handle is moved away from default.

contracts.text: `BlendRangeChannel.this_layer_black_split` boolean property exists.
`BlendRangeChannel.this_layer_white_split` boolean property exists.
`BlendRangeChannel.underlying_black_split` boolean property exists.
`BlendRangeChannel.underlying_white_split` boolean property exists.
Each split property is `True` when the corresponding slider's `left_handle != right_handle`, and `False` otherwise.
contracts.adverse_condition: A slider has differing handles (split state).

contracts.text: `BlendRangeChannel.describe()` returns a non-empty string.
`BlendRanges` class is defined in `psd_tools.api.blend_range`.
`BlendRanges` constructor takes `composite` (a `BlendRangeChannel`) and `channels` (a list of `BlendRangeChannel`).
Positional: the first argument to `BlendRanges` is stored as `composite` and the second as `channels`.
contracts.adverse_condition: `composite` and `channels` are distinguishable and the constructor is non-commutative.

contracts.text: `BlendRanges.channel_count` property exists.
`len(blend_ranges)` returns the number of channels only, not counting the composite channel.
contracts.adverse_condition: Composite is non-empty and channels list has a different count from composite-plus-channels total.

contracts.text: `BlendRanges` supports indexing (including negative indices) on channels only, not the composite.
contracts.adverse_condition: A negative index is used; composite exists and could be confused with a channel.

contracts.text: Iteration over a `BlendRanges` yields only the channel `BlendRangeChannel` objects, not the composite.
contracts.adverse_condition: Composite is present and channels are non-empty, so including composite in iteration would change the count.

contracts.text: `BlendRanges.from_raw(raw_blending_ranges)` classmethod exists, accepting a `LayerBlendingRanges` object.
`BlendRanges.from_channels(composite, channels)` classmethod exists.
Positional: in `from_channels`, the first argument maps to `composite` and the second to `channels`.
contracts.adverse_condition: `composite` and `channels` are distinguishable and non-commutative.

contracts.text: `BlendRanges.apply_to_raw(raw)` method exists.
`apply_to_raw(raw)` writes the blend range data back into the supplied raw object.
contracts.adverse_condition: The current blend range data differs from what is already in the raw object, so a no-op write would be detectable.

contracts.text: When `BlendRanges` is created from null/None raw ranges, `channels` is an empty list.
When `BlendRanges` is created from null/None raw ranges, `composite` defaults to full range.
`BlendRanges.is_default` property exists.
`is_default` returns `True` when all channels AND the composite are at their default positions.
`is_default` returns `False` when any channel or the composite is not at its default position.
contracts.adverse_condition: At least one channel or the composite is non-default.

contracts.text: `BlendRanges.describe()` returns a non-empty string.
`BlendRanges.compute_visibility(source_color, backdrop_color)` method exists.
`compute_visibility` accepts float arrays whose values are in [0, 1].
Positional: in `compute_visibility`, the first argument is `source_color` and the second is `backdrop_color`.
contracts.adverse_condition: `source_color` and `backdrop_color` are distinguishable arrays and the operation is non-commutative (e.g., "This Layer" sliders use source, "Underlying" use backdrop).

contracts.text: `compute_visibility` returns a weight array of shape `(H, W, 1)`.
contracts.adverse_condition: Input height H and width W differ (non-square), so an `(N, N, 1)` shape would be incorrect for one dimension.

contracts.text: Every element of the returned weight array is in the range [0, 1].
contracts.adverse_condition: Input values at boundaries 0.0 and 1.0; split sliders could produce intermediate weights.

contracts.text: `BlendRanges.to_pil_mask(source_color, backdrop_color)` method exists.
`to_pil_mask` returns a PIL `Image` in `'L'` mode.
`Layer` class gains a `blend_ranges` property.
The `blend_ranges` property on `Layer` persists through a save/load round-trip.
contracts.adverse_condition: `blend_ranges` is set to a non-default value before saving.

contracts.text: Writing `LayerBlendingRanges` validates that `composite_ranges` contains exactly 2 pairs, raising `ValueError` otherwise.
contracts.adverse_condition: `composite_ranges` has a number of pairs other than 2 (e.g., 0, 1, or 3).

contracts.text: Writing `LayerBlendingRanges` validates that each channel range contains exactly 2 pairs, raising `ValueError` otherwise.
contracts.adverse_condition: At least one channel range has a number of pairs other than 2.

contracts.text: The validation error raised on invalid pair counts is `ValueError`.
The compositing engine applies blend-if during layer composition.
contracts.adverse_condition: `blend_ranges` is set to a non-default value; default blend ranges would make the effect invisible.

contracts.text: The composite (gray) range modulates visibility based on the luminosity formula `0.299*R + 0.587*G + 0.114*B`.
contracts.adverse_condition: R, G, B channel values differ, so using equal weights would produce a different luminosity value.

contracts.text: Per-channel ranges modulate visibility based on individual channel values (R for red, G for green, B for blue), not luminosity.
contracts.adverse_condition: Per-channel ranges differ from the composite range, and individual channel values differ from the luminosity value.

contracts.text: The "This Layer" slider uses source color values for its visibility calculation.
contracts.adverse_condition: Source and backdrop colors differ, so swapping them would produce a different result.

contracts.text: The "Underlying Layer" slider uses backdrop color values for its visibility calculation.
contracts.adverse_condition: Backdrop and source colors differ, so swapping them would produce a different result.

contracts.text: Split sliders produce a linear fade (linear interpolation) between the left and right handle positions.
contracts.adverse_condition: A slider is split (left_handle ≠ right_handle); a non-split slider has a single threshold with no fade.

All work must be committed when done.
